summary: Customer is developing a hot polymer extrusion process incorporating an active pharmaceutical ingredient and wants to investigate whether an optical measurement can detect composition changes while the melt is being processed. They have offline assays, but the process interface is hot and may be exposed to material build up. They request an initial comparison plan and the questions required before choosing a probe.

unknowns: Target species and range: which composition changes must be detected and over what concentration or property range
Matrix and interferences: polymer type, API, additives, excipients, and other species that may absorb or scatter
Physical state and optical behaviour: whether the hot melt is clear, turbid, opaque, or opaque_absorbing at the measurement wavelength
Temperature and pressure: actual process temperature, pressure, and stability at the intended interface
Installation point and distance: where in the extrusion process the measurement would be made and the required standoff or window
Cleaning and fouling: build-up rate, material, cleaning method, and compatibility with the process interface
Required accuracy and response time: needed precision, detection limit, and temporal resolution for composition changes
Reference method: details of the offline assays, sampling, comparability, and uncertainty
Flow and mixing state: whether the melt composition is homogeneous at the measurement point
API stability and phase behaviour under process conditions
